papers.title: Native-hip survival after modified Chiari osteotomy and the outcome of conversion to total hip arthroplasty: a retrospective cohort study with a matched comparison
papers.abstract: Joint preservation in the young dysplastic hip aims to defer an arthroplasty that would otherwise carry a high lifetime revision burden. Whether the preceding osteotomy affects that arthroplasty is unclear, because the two have usually been reported in separate cohorts. We assessed both in one cohort. We reviewed 50 hips treated with a modified Chiari osteotomy for dysplasia or other childhood hip disease. The primary outcome was native-hip survival, estimated by Kaplan-Meier analysis with conversion to total hip arthroplasty (THA) as the endpoint. In an exploratory secondary analysis, conversion THAs were matched 1:2 with primary THAs by diagnosis, sex and operative year and compared by the post-THA modified Harris Hip Score (mHHS); operative details were compared between 18 conversion and 30 primary hips. Native-hip survival was 84.5% at 10 years and 55.5% at 20 years (95% confidence interval [CI] 37.1–74.0), and did not differ between dysplastic hips and those with Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease sequelae (log-rank p = 0.552). In preserved hips the mean mHHS improved from 55 to 72 (p < 0.001). Eighteen hips (36%) were converted at a median of 12.4 years. No significant difference in post-THA mHHS was detected between the conversion and primary groups (83.1 vs 84.7; difference − 1.5, 95% CI − 5.8 to 2.8), also after age adjustment. Operative time (110 vs 108 min) and blood loss (300 vs 300 mL) did not differ. More than half of the hips were still preserved 20 years after the osteotomy. When preservation failed, no significant difference in function was detected versus matched primary THA, and operative time, blood loss and the use of acetabular bone graft did not differ significantly, although this small exploratory comparison was not powered to establish equivalence. Native-hip survival after a Chiari osteotomy and the outcome of the arthroplasty that follows have almost always been reported in separate cohorts. This study follows one consecutive series through both phases, quantifying how long the native hip is retained and how the eventual arthroplasty performs early in the same patients.

papers.title: Design and theoretical assessment of Ti-Mo-Nb-Sn alloys for biomedical applications: a review
papers.abstract: Biomaterials include a wide range of materials, including metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites. Of these, metallic materials are the most widely used, with titanium and its alloys being chosen for the medical field, particularly in orthopedics and dentistry, owing to their favorable weight-to-strength ratio, high mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and biocompatibility. However, titanium in its pure form does not always provide an optimal compromise between strength, elastic modulus, and microstructural stability, so alloying with biocompatible elements is used to fine-tune its mechanical and biological properties. First- and second-generation titanium implant alloys nonetheless present recognized limitations, including an elastic modulus considerably higher than that of cortical bone, which produces stress shielding, and the potential toxicity of the Al and V alloying elements used in Ti-6Al-4V. These shortcomings have driven sustained interest in metastable β-type titanium alloys stabilized by non-toxic elements such as Mo, Nb, Ta, Zr, and Sn. This review reorganizes current knowledge of the Ti-Mo-Nb-Sn system around the requirements such an alloy must satisfy, the individual and combined roles of Mo, Nb, and Sn as β-stabilizers, the compositions reported in the literature, the structure-to-property relationships that govern their mechanical behavior, and the methods used to assess their corrosion resistance and biocompatibility, concluding with the principal research gaps and future perspectives for this alloy family. The reviewed studies reported elastic moduli of about 49–65 GPa for single-β compositions, with yield strengths comfortably surpassing 200 MPa, with values of 400–975 MPa. Data regarding the biological profile exists for only one composition, and more information is inferred from related ternary alloys. Windows of 4–6 Mo, 11–20 Nb, and 6–9 Sn wt.% looking promising, but fatigue, wear resistance and long-term biological data are missing.

papers.title: Optimizing AIS surgery with a digital twin framework integrating AI and personalized biomechanical modeling
papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose Posterior spinal fusion (PSF) is the primary treatment for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) curves >45°, yet planning remains largely radiographic and empirical, with limited integration of patient-specific biomechanics. AI and biomechanical modeling now offer opportunities for objective, personalized evaluation of instrumentation strategies. This study developed and evaluated a patient-specific model-based optimization framework combining AI-predicted instrumentation with deterministic physics-based biomechanical simulation to explore construct trade-offs within predefined computational constraints. Methods Twenty AIS patients (Lenke 1/2, age 12–19) treated with selective thoracic PSF were analyzed using data from the MIMO clinical trial. Patient-specific digital twin models were generated from validated 3D reconstructions and implemented in a multibody dynamic simulation environment. AI-predicted instrumentation parameters (UIV, LIV, screw number, rod curvature) were varied within clinical ranges, generating 972 construct configurations per patient (19,440 total simulations). A multi-objective optimization algorithm identified AI-derived strategies balancing 3D correction, screw pullout forces, and preservation of unfused vertebrae, which were compared with simulated surgeon-performed constructs. Simulated outcomes included MT Cobb angle, thoracic kyphosis, apical vertebral rotation, screw pullout force, number of screws, and fused levels. Strategies were compared using repeated-measures MANOVA. Results Optimized configurations achieved similar modeled 3D correction to surgeon-performed constructs, with a mean 3° greater coronal correction (95% CI [0.58, 5.81], p = .019) while maintaining comparable axial derotation (AVR) and thoracic kyphosis. Optimized strategies used fewer screws (mean reduction of 4, p < 0.001) and fewer fused levels (median reduction of 2, p < 0.001). All configurations remained within defined pullout force thresholds. Conclusion In this exploratory simulation study, integration of AI-derived instrumentation with a patient-specific digital twin framework combining deterministic physics-based biomechanical modeling and optimization identified alternative constructs using fewer screws and shorter fusion spans while maintaining broadly comparable modeled 3D correction and implant loading. The small differences in modeled correction should not be interpreted as evidence of clinical superiority, and prospective clinical validation is required.

papers.title: Efficiency of impact pendulum tests for road restraint systems: A review and evaluation
papers.abstract: Full-scale crash testing is the definitive approach for evaluating the crashworthiness of road restraint systems (RRS), but it requires specialised proving grounds, instrumented vehicles, extensive safety infrastructure, and substantial financial and logistical resources. Impact pendulum testing has therefore been widely used as a repeatable and comparatively economical surrogate during preliminary structural assessment, design development, and numerical-model validation. However, technical information on these systems remains dispersed across journal articles and technical reports. This review critically evaluates the application, capabilities, and limitations of impact pendulum systems for RRS and consolidates their principal design and testing characteristics. The study combines a bibliometric assessment of Scopus and Web of Science records updated through 2026, supported by VOSviewer analysis, with a detailed comparison of 29 RRS-related pendulum-system configurations identified in the literature. The systems were examined in terms of impactor material and geometry, mass, suspension arrangement, impact nose, impact height and angle, initial height, impact energy and velocity, instrumentation, performance indicators, applicable standards, and numerical simulation methods. The review shows substantial variation in pendulum design and test conditions, while rigid impactors, predominantly perpendicular impacts, and dynamic measurements using accelerometers, load cells, strain gauges, and displacement or velocity sensors are common features. LS-DYNA is the most frequently used numerical tool for calibrating and validating impact models. Overall, pendulum tests are particularly useful for structural-response screening, comparative assessment, component-level impact evaluation, and finite element model calibration and validation. Nevertheless, they cannot fully reproduce vehicle trajectory, occupant risk, post-impact stability, or the complete kinematics of oblique full-scale collisions and should not be regarded as a substitute for certification-level vehicle crash testing. Future research should prioritise standardised test procedures, adjustable impact conditions, more representative impactor configurations, and closer integration of pendulum experiments with validated numerical simulations, including applications addressing the evolving characteristics of electric vehicles.

papers.title: Simple Box-Cox probabilistic models for hourly streamflow predictions
papers.abstract: Abstract. The increasing availability of hourly scale hydrological data offers valuable benefits for advancing our scientific understanding of catchment processes and improving operational forecasting capabilities. This work contributes to streamflow predictions at the hourly scale by investigating practical methods for uncertainty quantification using probabilistic predictions. We examine common approaches for representing the heteroscedasticity of streamflow errors using the Box-Cox (BC) transformation and common approaches for representing the persistence of streamflow errors using auto-regressive (AR) models. Case studies based on 7 catchments from Spain, Switzerland and USA that cover humid to semi-arid conditions are reported. The results favor Box-Cox transformations with power parameter values of 0–0.5. Notably the log transformation achieves the best statistical reliability of predictions, while its precision and volumetric bias are not statistically significantly worse than for the BC02 and BC05 transformations respectively. The results also tend to favor the AR2 and AR3 models over the AR1 model in representing persistence of errors, with the addition of moving average terms providing little additional benefit. The study findings are broadly consistent with earlier work with daily data, and provide practical guidance for hourly scale studies in predictive uncertainty quantification that is accessible to a wide range of hydrologists. We also report progress towards "seamless" aggregation from hourly to longer scales, which is a capability that is desirable in many practical operational contexts.

papers.title: Rheological optimization of low-methylated pectin–xyloglucan–cellulose nanocrystal composites for 3D printing: stability and printability
papers.abstract: Abstract Extrusion-based 3D printing of biobased hydrogels depends on ink rheology, requiring strong shear-thinning for smooth flow and sufficient yield stress to maintain shape after deposition. Polysaccharides from plant cell walls (PCW) are known as sustainable, structurally stable materials, but their three main components—cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectin—have not been combined for this purpose. Here, a bioink composed of cellulose nanocrystals, xyloglucan, and pectin is developed for extrusion printing using response surface methodology (RSM) with material characterization. Systematic variation in composition reveals clear relationships between rheology, print fidelity, and mechanical performance. FTIR confirms composition-dependent hydrogen bonding within inks and printed structures, along with formulation-dependent colour changes. Among the components, pectin has the strongest influence on rheology. Biobased inks with equal proportions of all three components (3% and 5%) show optimal printability. Compared to 3%, 5% formulations exhibit higher viscosity and yield stress, improving shape retention and pore definition. Ionic cross-linking does not significantly affect geometry but enhances mechanical strength. These findings highlight multicomponent plant polysaccharide inks as tunable, sustainable materials for extrusion-based additive manufacturing, mimicking natural PCW assembly.

papers.title: Physics-informed symbolic regression for predicting the glass transition temperature of alkali borate glasses
papers.abstract: The glass transition temperature ( T g ) of alkali borate glasses is strongly composition-dependent and difficult to predict from first principles due to the structural complexity of the boron network. Here, we apply physics-informed symbolic regression (combining evolutionary search with physically meaningful descriptors) to derive an interpretable closed-form expression for T g for the x M 2 O ⋅ ( 100 − x ) B 2 O 3 glass family, with M = Li, Na and K, and x expressed in mol%, followed by extrapolation to M = Rb and Cs. The resulting model achieves a root mean square error of 14–16 K while maintaining clear physical interpretability, explicitly capturing the interplay among T g , structural dissociation energy, and network packing. Critically, models built on the Rigid Unit Packing Fraction (RUPF) yield substantially more realistic T g predictions than those using the conventional Atomic Packing Fraction (APF), as APF overestimates structural rigidity at intermediate compositions. The fitted dissociation energies are further validated against the revised Makishima–Mackenzie model, confirming that the inferred parameters are physically consistent, not merely statistically effective, within the alkali borate family. Finally, Monte Carlo uncertainty quantification reveals that prediction uncertainty is highest in the compositional regions associated with the boron anomaly, directly linking model limitations to a known structural transition in these glasses. This result highlights the potential of physics-informed symbolic regression as a transparent and interpretable alternative to black-box models for property prediction in glass systems.

papers.title: Development of solid reinforced porous femoral components made using electron beam powder bed fusion to meet endurance requirement
papers.abstract: Abstract Solid stemmed femoral components are currently used, although they can be porous-coated. A highly porous component can enhance the long-term fixation of the implant through bone in-growth. Electron beam powder bed fusion (EBPBF) is capable of fabricating porous structures. However, a femoral component also needs to function under a highly critical loading condition. In this study, design/simulation, EBPBF and fatigue testing were conducted in order to develop satisfactory and highly porous Ti6Al4V femoral components. Loading during testing has closely followed that set by the international standard for femoral components. After the initial design, EBPBF and testing, a final design was made through topological optimisation and components were made. Tests have shown that two components have satisfied the requirement well (cycle number N > 5 x10 7 ) and two have failed each with a failure cycle number (N f ) slightly lower in logarithmic scale than the required (N f >5 x10 6 cycles). Then, an attempt has been made to explain the effect of EBPBF defect on N f using the Kitagawa-Takahashi (K-T) diagram approach through (a) tests to determine the threshold stress intensity factor, (b) fractography and micro-CT to locate the defects and measure the defect sizes, (c) close evaluation of stress in defect locations by simulation. It has been shown that the effect of defects affecting N f in a real component could approximately, although not highly accurately, be explained using the K-T diagram approach. The present findings may suggest how highly porous EMPBF femoral components can be designed, built and quality assured to satisfy the fatigue life requirement.

papers.title: Design and Implementation of Energy Digital Twin System for Railway Stations
papers.abstract: Building energy simulation relies on static design-stage inputs and diverges from actual operation after commissioning. This study designs a railway-station digital twin system in five layers, coupling measurements with simulation without re-exporting the model by combining pyenergyplus.api and eppy, and implements it for railway station. The system assembles an EnergyPlus model from a generation script and a parameter catalogue, modifies envelope, equipment and schedules at the object level with eppy, and runs EnergyPlus 26.1.0 in-process, completing an annual simulation of the ten-zone station model in 3.8 to 6.1 seconds. The model was calibrated to monthly metered electricity within ASHRAE Guideline 14 monthly criteria, and CO2 measured by the on-site sensor network was inverted through a mass balance to update ventilation and occupancy inputs. The service layer serves parametric queries via FastAPI, Celery, a result cache, an XGBoost surrogate and Bayesian optimization, and a web dashboard provides monitoring and scenario exploration. The core API and worker processes ran 27 days from 5 August 2026 without restart. Parametric analysis and measurement coupling are achieved in one environment without the re-export required by the earlier FMU approach, while per-timestep measurement injection and closed-loop updating remain at the design stage with interfaces implemented.

papers.title: Empowering Digital Twins with Generative AI: Applications, Case Studies, and Limitations
papers.abstract: Abstract The rise of the Generative Pre-Trained Transformer(GPT) language model, more commonly used as ChatGPT, has brought a spotlight on the ever-developing field of Generative AI (GAI). With current advancements in graphics processing units (GPUs), training and using deep generative models have become easier. Similarly, the developments in edge computing have made it possible to make the most of GAI’s potential for numerous use cases. One such use case involves its integration with Digital Twin technology, offering new possibilities for enhanced simulations, predictive analytics, and real-time decision-making. This paper explores the prospects of combining GAI with Digital Twin technology to create innovative solutions for applications like healthcare, manufacturing, agriculture, cybersecurity, etc. It also discusses how GAI can train Digital Twins by simulating various scenarios and providing different data sets, enabling predictive maintenance. It also delves into the real-world scenarios in which the technology has been implemented. The paper concludes with the limitations of GAI technology for Digital Twin applications, which can be worked upon in the future.

papers.title: Optimal Day-Ahead Dispatch of a Grid-Connected Microgrid with Energy Storage under Time-of-Use Pricing and Load Uncertainty
papers.abstract: Microgrid energy management must balance a time-of-use electricity purchase plan against battery storage dispatch so that the total purchase cost is minimised while all physical constraints on state of charge and charge/discharge power are satisfied. Existing studies rely onnonlinear economic model predictive control orrolling-horizon optimisation, which restore feasibility online but do not guarantee a global optimum, and onprice-arbitrage battery scheduling that treats the tariff in isolation. Model constructs a two-stage framework that first partitions the tariff into three tiers by partitioning-around-medoids clustering with a silhouette coefficient of 0.772 and then solves a deterministic day-ahead dispatch with linear programming and an equivalent big-M mixed-integer program, which yields a globally optimal schedule with zero simultaneous charge/discharge slots. Day-ahead uncertainty is absorbed by a quantile safety margin plus penalised emergency purchase. The deterministic scheme lowers the daily purchase cost from 48,052.05 to 35,126.95 yuan, a 26.90% saving, and the annual two-stage cost is 14,066,913.87 yuan. Compared with online controllers, the model offers a global optimum guarantee, an explicit three-tier price interpretation, and atractable safety margin.

papers.title: From Irrigation Prescriptions to Verified Water Delivery: Actuation-Aware MPC and Digital Twins for Moving Variable-Rate Sprinkler Systems
papers.abstract: Variable-rate irrigation (VRI) prescribes spatially differentiated water demand. A moving sprinkler implements these prescriptions through travel speed, valve duty, pressure, and timing. This review examines how model predictive control (MPC), state estimation, sprinkler hydraulics, application measurement, and digital twins can support the conversion of a prescription into verified water delivery. Evidence, classified by function and validation setting, distinguishes direct irrigation MPC studies from transferable sensing, modeling, and equipment evidence. Irrigation MPC has progressed from soil water regulation toward forecast-, risk-, crop-value-, and space-informed prescriptions. Verification of machine-level delivery combines explicit execution models with independent measurements. Field and bench studies show that motion, pressure, valve timing, nozzle geometry, footprint overlap, and wind constrain delivery and its measurement, while independent application feedback remains uncommon. The review proposes a command-to-delivery sequence comprising actuation time demand, projection onto the machine-attainable field, and separate residuals for projection, command tracking, and application transfer. A control-coupled digital twin is proposed as a testable layer preserving time alignment, model versioning, and residual provenance, and translating supported updates into feasible actions or safe degradation. The proposed future evaluation pathway comprises independently measured delivery and claim-matched ablation, with multi-season trials for interannual benefit claims and representative fault tests for resilience claims.

papers.title: A contraction-constrained distributed MPC for heterogeneous vehicle platoons with explicit string stability
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous vehicle platoons with nonlinear dynamics make it difficult to translate frequency-domain string-stability metrics into constraints that can be enforced online. To address this issue, this paper proposes a contraction-constrained distributed model predictive control strategy for heterogeneous platoons. In each local optimization problem, a time-domain contraction inequality is introduced to bound the finite-horizon mismatch between the predicted and assumed spacing-error trajectories. Together with the established closed-loop conditions, the resulting contraction mechanism provides an explicit, solver-embeddable route to predecessor-wise peak-error non-amplification. A terminal constraint set is further incorporated to guarantee asymptotic consensus, and sufficient conditions for recursive feasibility and string stability are established via Lyapunov analysis. Comparative simulations against a baseline that removes the contraction constraint demonstrate that the proposed strategy effectively suppresses spacing-error amplification under acceleration, deceleration, and multi-stage speed-change scenarios, while maintaining stable performance under platoon-size scaling.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Wind Energy Forecasting with Emphasis on Complex Terrain: A Structured Review of Automated Architecture Search, Data Fusion, Uncertainty Quantification, and Explainability
papers.abstract: Wind energy forecasting in complex terrain is a critical challenge for reliable power grid integration. This PRISMA 2020-guided structured review examines 134 eligible studies (2018–2026) that apply deep learning (DL) and other neural-network methods to wind speed forecasting, wind power prediction, and wind field downscaling, with particular emphasis on complex terrain. Four methodological pillars are analyzed: automated deep learning (AutoDL/NAS), multi-source data fusion, uncertainty quantification with emphasis on conformal prediction, and explainable AI (XAI). Only 24 studies (18%) explicitly evaluate mountainous, valley, coastal, or urban settings. CNN-based models are the most frequent architecture family, whereas AutoDL/NAS and automated hyperparameter optimization appear in only 11 studies, and no NAS framework has been evaluated in complex terrain. Reported fusion gains are study-specific (from about 13% RMSE reduction to over 50% MAE reduction) and are not directly comparable across datasets, metrics, and baselines. Conformal prediction offers finite-sample coverage guarantees under exchangeability, yet its empirical reliability under terrain-induced non-stationarity has not been evaluated. XAI appears in only five DL studies and is mostly applied post hoc. No study combines three or more pillars. We identify ten challenges and propose ten future directions toward integrated, terrain-aware, uncertainty-calibrated, and interpretable forecasting frameworks.

papers.title: Active Learning for Probabilistic Safety Assessment of Adjacent Floating Bodies under Extreme Wave Loadings
papers.abstract: Abstract Probabilistic safety assessment of adjacent floating bodies under extreme waves requires accurate estimation of structural failure probability, which is hampered by strongly nonlinear hydrodynamic coupling and prohibitive simulation costs. This study develops an active-learning framework that couples a high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics numerical wave tank with Gaussian-process surrogate modeling and wave-group parameterization, achieving converged failure-probability estimates with fewer simulations than direct Monte Carlo. Applied to a simplified two-body system under a 100-year return-period sea state, the framework reveals a nonmonotonic dependence of failure probability on the gap-to-breadth ratio G / D , with minimum risk at G / D = 0.5 and increasing risk at wider spacings due to progressive interbody phase decoupling. Sensitivity analyses across multiple failure thresholds confirm the robustness of this trend.

papers.title: THE IMPACT OF INTERACTIVE DIGITAL STORYTELLING ON LEARNER ENGAGEMENT IN HIGHER EDUCATION HUMANITIES COURSES
papers.abstract: The main aim of this research is to explore how Interactive Digital Storytelling (IDS) can transform traditional teaching methods and enhance student engagement in higher education, particularly in the arts and humanities. The study employed a systematic literature review (SLR) guided by the PRISMA 2020 framework to synthesise existing evidence on the relationship between IDS and student engagement. A systematic search of peer-reviewed literature published between January 2020 and July 2025 was conducted across Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC, Education Source, IEEE Xplore, SpringerLink, and Google Scholar. Relevant studies were identified using predefined keywords and Boolean search strategies and were selected according to predetermined inclusion and exclusion criteria. Following the removal of duplicate records, titles and abstracts were screened, and full-text articles were assessed for relevance, methodological quality, and eligibility. Any disagreements between reviewers were resolved through discussion or consultation with a third reviewer. The selected studies were synthesised thematically and grouped according to subject area to identify patterns and evidence concerning the role of IDS in enhancing students' behavioural, cognitive, and emotional engagement. The findings indicate that IDS can increase students' interest, motivation, participation, knowledge retention, and emotional connection to learning. The integration of decision-making elements, multimedia resources, and contextualised information can promote active learning, critical thinking, and deeper understanding of subject content. However, the effectiveness of IDS depends on institutional readiness, including the availability of adequate technological infrastructure, educators' digital competencies, and effective curriculum integration. The reviewed literature also highlights challenges related to unequal levels of digital literacy, cognitive and emotional demands, accessibility, and the resources required for the development and implementation of IDS. This research contributes to the growing body of scholarship on technology-enhanced learning in the arts and humanities by demonstrating that IDS can function not only as a tool for increasing student engagement but also as a pedagogical framework for facilitating collaborative knowledge construction. It is recommended that IDS initiatives prioritise accessibility and inclusive design, alignment with educational objectives and user needs, targeted professional development for educators, and equitable institutional investment in digital learning technologies. These findings have implications for curriculum designers, educators, educational planners, and higher education decision-makers. Future research should examine the long-term effects of IDS on knowledge acquisition and retention, its applicability across diverse educational contexts, and its integration with emerging technologies such as virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR) to further enhance student engagement.

papers.title: Study on flow and heat transfer characteristics of a D-type triple-period minimal surface heat exchanger
papers.abstract: Abstract Rising thermal loads in aircraft engines and onboard systems demand efficient compact heat exchangers. D-type three-period minimal surface (TPMS) offers high specific surface area, smooth continuous surfaces, and favorable parametric design. We numerically study flow and thermal behavior in a D-type TPMS heat exchanger, focusing on vortex evolution, heat-transfer intensification, and asymmetric hot/cold channel responses to hot-side velocity. Periodic D-type geometry generates four vortex tubes at flow junctions. Their downstream re-pairing enhances radial mixing and disrupts thermal boundary layers, maintaining large wall temperature gradients and improving heat transfer but causing flow losses. Wall heat flux depends jointly on both streams. Increasing hot-side inlet velocity strengthens hot-side convection but deteriorates cold-side heat transfer due to higher near-wall temperature and thickened cold-side boundary layers. j-F factor quantifies the trade-off: higher hot-side velocity boosts convection yet amplifies pressure penalty, lowering efficiency under asymmetric flow. This reveals flow–heat coupling mechanisms for aerospace thermal management.

papers.title: Deterministic cellular automata, probabilistic observations: quotient measurement by embedded observers
papers.abstract: In the cellular-automaton programme for quantum mechanics (including 't Hooft's Cellular Automaton Interpretation and related Hamiltonian-automaton and stochastic-clock approaches), a core question still awaiting operationalization is how to define, inside the automaton, a subsystem that acts as an observer — how measurement is physically implemented, and how an embedded subsystem can operate at an effective resolution below the global update rate. We define an observer by its registration loop rather than by labelled cells: a local process counts as part of an observer S iff it enters S's registration, comparison, maintenance, or response-selection loop. S is a proper subset of the system it inhabits, with no cost-free access to resources beyond itself; since registering a difference requires holding a current item against a maintained contrast item, the distinctions S can concurrently maintain within one operational step are bounded by a registration capacity C(S). Measurement is then a finite map , inducing a partition on configuration space. A resolution asymmetry follows: S can register, at full grain, structures generated more coarsely than itself, but not structures as fine as itself — including any domain containing S, whose registration is a registration of S's own distinction structure (a second-order, self-referential measurement). Since S cannot internally generate a strict refinement of , on the full-grain self-referential task is necessarily non-injective relative to any finer comparison standpoint: a forced, internally undetectable coarse-graining (a quotient) — S cannot tell from a registered value whether its preimage is one fine-grained configuration or several. Other-directed quotienting is conditional, occurring when the target's grain outruns the observer's resolving grain or when concurrent maintenance demand exceeds C(S); self-directed quotienting is unconditional at the resolution level; and any finer standpoint invoked here is itself finite. Information thus forms only downstream of resolvability and concurrent maintenance: what S holds is either a full-grain registration or a quotient — never the pre-registration event structure itself. Two consequences follow. Probability need not enter the update rule: the substrate remains deterministic, in line with the Cellular Automaton Interpretation, while for the embedded observer probabilistic description appears as a normalized valuation on the quotient outcome space — classes corresponding to preimages it cannot unfold — a natural operational form for registration under insufficient capacity, offering a complementary, registration-level route to stochastic-clock-type behaviour. And a "slower observer" requires no modified dynamics: slowness is a property of registration structure — step size, operational window, concurrent capacity — not of the update rule. A minimal simulation can make the contrast between the two standpoints explicit: the modeller reads the full configuration and lattice structure cost-free within the simulation, while the embedded observer holds only the quotient induced by its capacity — a standpoint unavailable to any physical observer. Measurement is thus constitutive rather than read-out. All results follow from counting and partition arguments, independent of the specific update rule.

papers.title: ‘Entering a Forbidden Territory’: Co-Creation of Assessment Marking Criteria
papers.abstract: Advancements in active learning methods necessitate transparent and continuous dialogue between learners and educators to align and reconcile differing expectations. This study investigates the co-creation of assessment marking criteria in higher education, emphasising the pedagogical value of involving learners in collaboratively designing rubrics with teachers. The research explores how co-creation fosters student engagement, critical thinking, and shared ownership of valuable active learning opportunities. Conducted following a postgraduate module, the study analysed learners’ experiences of co-creating a marking rubric and employed a qualitative methodology involving module evaluations, focus groups, and interviews with participating learners. Four key themes emerged from the data on student perceptions of co-creating a marking rubric in that they: provided novel learning experiences, enhanced agency and creativity, strengthened the sense of community, and improved clarity of assessment expectations for authentic assessment. Benefits and challenges in rubric co-design and implementation are discussed within each of these themes. Findings reveal that 82% of participating learners reported a greater understanding of assessment criteria, with several describing the co-creation process as transformative and one likening the experience to ‘entering a forbidden territory’. The collaborative development of the rubric promoted inclusivity, deepened assessment literacy, and enhanced learners’ confidence and motivation. Findings also suggest that the experience of co-creating the marking rubric may have contributed to higher student achievement in the associated summative assessment task. The research demonstrates that co-creating assessment rubrics can not only enhance academic performance but also build a more inclusive, student-centred educational environment. These findings support broader implementation of co-creation practices as a means to enrich active learning and foster collaborative academic communities.

papers.title: MAGNET-GEN: A Lakatosian, Pre-registered Research Programme for the Accelerated Design of Rare-Earth-Free Permanent Magnets — Phases, Articulations, Falsification Results and VV&UQ Assessment
papers.abstract: Europe imports about 98% of its permanent magnets from a single supplier country, at the very moment when the Critical Raw Materials Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1252) imposes benchmarks of 10% extraction, 40% processing and 25% recycling by 2030, and when successive Chinese export-control announcements (No. 18 of 4 April 2025; Nos. 55–58 and 61–62 of 9 October 2025; suspension No. 70 of 7 November 2025, expiring on 10 November 2026) have turned rare-earth supply into an instrument of industrial policy. This preprint reports a complete, auditable research campaign — MAGNET-GEN — that subjects a three-level, physics-informed quantum modelling paradigm for the accelerated design of permanent magnets to the discipline of a Lakatosian research programme: a sealed antecedence gate (P0) with a mechanical scoring function, pre-registered falsification tests executed exclusively on real, publicly identified datasets (Zenodo 23361847; Mendeley Data 10.17632/rvxsxsy9yw.2), verification–validation–uncertainty-quantification (VV&UQ) after Thacker et al. (2004) and Roy and Oberkampf (2011), and verdicts that were never adjusted a posteriori. Of the five sealed hypotheses, two were stopped at the gate by documentary antecedence, one was reformulated, and two progressed. Of the seven computational tests, three were refuted (mean-field Curie temperatures, Stoner–Wohlfarth hysteresis, out-of-distribution transfer) and four were not refuted (a 76-feature ridge surrogate, R² = 0.824; finite-size scaling of the 3D Ising model, Tc(∞) = 4.5071 ± 0.0412 against the reference 4.5115, a 0.10% deviation; residual-bootstrap uncertainty quantification, 90.5% coverage; bibliographic anchoring on 70 sourced values). Sealed re-tests confirmed the out-of-distribution failure (H-E2, H-F2) and validated a ferrite extension (H-G2). The campaign yields two patent technical notes (twenty claims each), a costed TRL-5 acceleration plan (T1–T4, €58,340, six weeks), and an application form for the Horizon Europe topic HORIZON-CL4-2027-01-MAT-PROD-06. The scientific contribution is twofold: a demonstrated methodology that makes a materials-modelling programme falsifiable end-to-end, and a quantified map of what survives falsification — and what does not — in data-driven coercivity prediction. Keywords: permanent magnets; rare-earth-free magnets; coercivity; Lakatosian research programme; falsification; pre-registration; verification, validation and uncertainty quantification (VV&UQ); machine learning; out-of-distribution generalisation; micromagnetism; Ising model; Critical Raw Materials Act; technological sovereignty. Version 2 (extended), November 2026 — 92 pages, 11 figures, 6 tables. Preprint prepared for arXiv submission.

papers.title: ŊHÏORYŪM: Optimal Linear Query Cubes for Affine Fourier Learning—Certified Measurement Compilation, Nuisance Cancellation, and Adaptive Cross-Task Acquisition
papers.abstract: This research release develops and evaluates a compiler that learns how to measure subsequent learning tasks from previously acquired spectral structure. In a synthetic active-query setting, measured feature dictionaries determine an affine family of Walsh-Fourier frequencies over GF(2). The compiler transforms that learned representation into explicit intervention directions, nuisance-cancelling parity stencils, coefficient readouts, and independently audited acceptance decisions. The resulting procedure can recover interaction features absent from its acquisition dictionaries, including families whose features share no literal input coordinate. The central contribution connects an exact characterization of minimum full linear query cubes to executable measurement programs and acquisition-inclusive empirical comparisons. The work addresses researchers in active learning, learning theory, experimental design, program synthesis, Fourier analysis, representation transfer, and verifiable learning-system improvement. The observation model combines a sparse high-degree Walsh component, an unknown nuisance of degree at most \(q\), and fresh independent Gaussian noise. For an admitted affine frequency family of rank \(r\), the manuscript proves that a full linear query cube identifying that family while separating it from the nuisance requires at least \(r+q+1\) independent axes. Equality holds if and only if \(q+1\) pairwise disjoint odd checks exist for the affine family. Exact witnesses generate a construction attaining this bound. Explicit obstruction examples distinguish high-degree feature structure from the stronger conditions required for a minimum-size design. The emitted program includes a canonical affine origin and basis, parity witnesses, dual query directions, normalization, and the mapping from transformed observations to output frequencies. Its contracts establish nuisance cancellation and orthogonal coefficient recovery. In the specified dense, known-correct-envelope Gaussian model, coefficient noise variance is \(\sigma^2/Q\), and dense minimax risk at the stated orthogonal readout budgets is \(2^r\sigma^2/Q\). Here, \(Q\) counts raw readout observations. This estimation result has a different scope from the query-cube identifiability theorem and the sparse, unknown-structure learning experiments. A bounded alternative remains available when the minimum design cannot be constructed. If every frequency in the complete affine closure satisfies the declared degree type \(q<|a|\le K\), its rank is at most \(K\), and its active-coordinate union contains at most \(2K\) coordinates. A full active-coordinate cube therefore requires at most \(4^K\) readout points. Exact type and budget checks govern deployment; an unsuccessful numerical search remains inconclusive rather than becoming a nonexistence claim. Inference receives public model bounds and oracle access. Hidden coordinate-pair labels, true supports, coefficients, and true signal counts remain within teacher generation and post-decision evaluation. Learned structure determines the measurement program, while every subsequent teacher supplies fresh coefficient observations and original-space risk evidence. This verification is necessary because off-envelope signals can alias perfectly on specialized measurements. The acceptance target is high-degree component mean-square error at most 0.0625 under uniform Boolean inputs, equivalent to component error-norm tolerance 0.25. A rank-saturation rule reduces acquisition: training stops after the first certified dictionary when its typed affine hull reaches the public rank ceiling; otherwise, the protocol acquires a second task. Rejected specialized predictors trigger a paid generic fallback. Under the declared model, noise, and numerical assumptions, the two-branch acceptance protocol allocates a false-issuance budget of at most 0.05 per teacher. This is a task-level guarantee, not one simultaneous 95% guarantee across the benchmark. On the main 72-task matrix, spanning six latent world/dimension contexts in 64 and 256 input dimensions, the rank-stopped affine compiler certifies all 72 outputs using 2,151,872 observations, including 505,280 acquisition observations. A one-task learned active-coordinate estimator certifies the same 72 outputs using 2,644,224 observations, including 364,544 acquisition observations. The affine procedure uses approximately 18.6% fewer training-inclusive deployment observations on this workload. The difference includes representation adequacy and acquisition policy as well as specialized readout size. The preceding fixed-two-task protocol uses 2,404,736 total observations, compared with 3,608,064 for the supplied generic R5 comparator, with 72/72 certified outputs for both. Recorded transfer includes 261 recovered signal-feature occurrences absent from the acquisition dictionaries. Historical acquisition prefixes reused by the follow-up comparison are explicitly identified and charged. On 24 alternative-world cases, adaptive affine and active-coordinate totals are 871,808 and 893,568 observations, respectively, with 24/24 certified outputs for each: approximately 2.44% fewer observations. These case specifications had already appeared in an earlier probe study, so this comparison is not an untouched blind holdout. Higher-noise, shifted-family, zero-history probe, and short mixed-family workloads retain explicit cost-negative results. The main 512-point specialized readout excludes acquisition, audit, and fallback costs; these observation counts do not establish a hardware-independent wall-clock speedup. The reproducibility package includes the manuscript, proofs, executable compilers and controller, task factories, generated query programs, protocols, source-bound outcomes, negative controls, audit tools, and reproduction commands. Structured Parquet tables and lossless JSONL mirrors contain 668 evaluation records and 41 warmup usages, accompanied by 74 accounting contexts. These cover 148 distinct future teacher definitions and 21 distinct acquisition teacher definitions. Reused cases, competing methods, and shared acquisition prefixes are linked explicitly. The final audit covers 709 model-risk records, with no observed false certificate. The scientific release reports 73 passing operational tests, finite mathematical checks, seeded within-session replays, and 5,289 current source-hash checks. papers.title: Data-Driven Discovery of High-Performance EOR Surfactants: Coupling Molecular Dynamics with Active Learning
papers.abstract: Abstract Chemical Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR) is a central route to maximizing hydrocarbon recovery from mature reservoirs. Although its field-scale success depends on several factors─including surfactant cost, adsorption and retention on the reservoir rock, solubility, and phase behavior─achieving a low oil–water interfacial tension (IFT) is a key enabling requirement. However, the design of surfactants meeting this requirement is impeded by the vast combinatorics of the chemical space and the prohibitive cost of traditional trial-and-error screening. In this study, we present a synergistic materials informatics framework that integrates Machine Learning (ML) and Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations within an Active Learning (AL) workflow to accelerate surfactant discovery. Unlike static screening approaches, our methodology utilizes MD simulations as a high-fidelity oracle, iteratively labeling a subset of candidates to update a regressor, enabling the identification of high-performance surfactants from the PubChem database. Through this workflow, we identified Dodecylammonium Chloride (DDACl) as a top candidate; subsequent high-fidelity MD simulations confirmed a very low IFT at maximum surface coverage, outperforming widely used analogs such as Cetyltrimethylammonium Bromide (CTAB). We validated these computational findings through experimental tensiometry, confirming the efficacy of DDACl in reducing IFT in several oils with varying API gravities. The convergence of theoretical predictions with experimental results underscores the power of this data-driven framework to overcome the “small data” bottleneck in materials science, offering a scalable pathway for the data-driven discovery of surfactants with low oil–water IFT as candidates for EOR formulation development.

papers.title: Algorithms for a Layered Heterogeneous Plate Under Sliding and Loading Conditions with an AI-Based PINN Extension
papers.abstract: This study examines the effect of material heterogeneities and other structural factors on the dispersion of shear waves across a composite structure via two algorithms. The resulting dispersion relation is sought analytically and further examined numerically through the first algorithm. In addition, the study establishes a sensitivity analysis algorithm using an absolute normalized sensitivity procedure within the low-frequency spectrum, revealing the most sensitive parameters governing the overall dynamic response of the structure. In particular, for the benchmark rigidity, density and thickness ratios, the phase speed of the first mode is lowered by the skin heterogeneity in all three profiles when the foundation and sliding parameters are absent, most strongly for the quadratic profile (Type II); in the presence of a soft foundation and a sliding interface, the dependence on the heterogeneity parameter is no longer monotone for the exponential and hyperbolic profiles. Increasing the foundational stiffness enhances wave dispersion in the composite plate, whereas increasing the sliding contact parameter decreases shear wave dispersion. Regarding parameter sensitivity, evaluated locally on the dispersion curve, the stiffness of the foundation is found to be the most sensitive parameter for all three heterogeneity profiles. Furthermore, the analytically derived dispersion relations and absolute normalized sensitivity algorithms proposed herein serve as a physics-based foundation for machine learning approaches—specifically for training data generation and feature importance calibration—in the inverse characterization of layered inhomogeneous structures. Finally, a surrogate-initialized physics-informed neural network (PINN) and a data-driven surrogate network are formulated and, for the benchmark case of homogeneous layers with perfect bonding and traction-free outer faces, where a closed-form relation exists, are checked mode by mode against the exact dispersion relation (mean absolute error in frequency: 2.4×10−6 for the PINN at five wavenumbers and 1.4×10−2 for the surrogate over 0≤K≤1). Their extension to heterogeneous, sliding and loaded configurations is not demonstrated here and is left for future work.

papers.title: Machine-learning-enabled computational–experimental framework for structure–property mapping in TPMS lattice structures
papers.abstract: Abstract Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) lattice structures present significant potential for lightweight mechanical systems; however, property-driven design is constrained by the computational expense of repeated finite-element (FE) simulations and the substantial experimental effort required to establish reliable structure–property relationships. This study introduces a computationally efficient and interpretable framework for predicting Young’s modulus and specific stiffness in TPMS lattice structures, integrating surrogate modeling, inverse design, SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations)-based interpretation, and Bayesian optimization (BO) to efficiently identify high-performing designs, with experimental validation through additive manufacturing and mechanical testing. Seven machine learning models were evaluated on a dataset of 270 FE-simulated TPMS lattices spanning five topological families. The Stacked Ensemble (SE), combining Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), and Deep Neural Network predictors via a Ridge regression meta-learner, achieved the highest predictive accuracy (R² = 0.995 for Young’s modulus; R² = 0.997 for specific stiffness), while GPR demonstrated comparable performance. Both models generalized effectively to unseen designs with errors below 3% and were applied to inverse design, SHAP-based geometry–property interpretation, and Bayesian optimization. The framework identified target-satisfying geometries with errors below 1.1% and explored a design space of 4.47 × 10⁸ configurations in under three hours. Experimental validation confirmed Young’s modulus predictions within 3–16%, while specific stiffness deviations between 37 and 72% were attributed to fabrication-induced density increases rather than surrogate model limitations. The proposed framework offers a scalable, interpretable, robust, and experimentally validated pathway for rapid, property-driven TPMS lattice design.

papers.title: Teaching Philosophy in Nursing Education
papers.abstract: Teaching in nursing education extends beyond the delivery of theoretical knowledge; it involves developing competent, reflective, and compassionate nursing professionals who can respond effectively to the evolving demands of healthcare. This teaching philosophy outlines an approach to creating a supportive, inclusive, and engaging learning environment that promotes students’ academic and professional development. It is guided by six principles: integrating theoretical knowledge with clinical practice, evidence-based education, student-centred and active learning, reflective practice and continuous professional development, inclusivity, and a safe learning environment. Bridging classroom learning and clinical practice is emphasized through skills laboratories, simulation-based activities, case studies, and authentic clinical experiences. Evidence-informed teaching strategies and active student participation are considered important for strengthening critical thinking, clinical reasoning, problem-solving, and decision-making. Reflection, constructive feedback, and individualized academic support are encouraged to address diverse learning needs and promote lifelong learning. This philosophy recognizes that every student can develop professionally when provided with appropriate guidance, encouragement, and learning opportunities. Its ultimate aim is to prepare nursing graduates who demonstrate clinical competence, professional accountability, empathy, and a commitment to safe, evidence-based, and patient-centered care.

papers.title: Sampling-free Monte Carlo dropout approximation for single-pass uncertainty quantification in deep learning-based PET reconstructions
papers.abstract: Abstract Objective: Medical image reconstructions using deep learning (DL) can rapidly generate high-quality images from degraded measurements, but their clinical adoption remains challenging, largely due to the lack of fast and reliable methods to quantify aleatoric (data-driven) and epistemic (model-driven) uncertainties on a per-prediction basis. We aim to develop a computationally efficient approach for estimating both uncertainties at the voxel level in DL-based image reconstruction within a single inference run. Approach: We present a moment propagation-based framework that analytically approximates the conventional, multi-realization Monte Carlo (MC) dropout by propagating feature-map means and marginal variances through network layers, followed by a pre-calibrated correction table to compensate for covariance effects omitted in the approximation. This enables joint estimation of reconstruction, aleatoric uncertainty and epistemic uncertainty in a single forward pass. The proposed framework was implemented on top of FastPET -- a network model synthesizing PET reconstructions from time-of-flight histo-images -- and evaluated in a patient pilot study of 26 total-body PET/CT acquisitions (16 [18F]-FDG and 10 [18F]-PSMA cases). Main Results: Proposed method achieved relatively strong agreement with the 50-pass MC approach, with absolute differences <0.5% for reconstruction, <4.2% for aleatoric uncertainty and <9.8% for epistemic uncertainty, along with narrow spreads across patients and tracer types, while reducing computation time by ~40-fold. In a complementary proof-of-concept low-count experiment, regional tracer uptake confidence intervals (CIs, derived from propagated uncertainties) widened with increased noise level, and reference uptakes consistently fell close to CI boundaries, indicating the proposed method could provide roughly calibrated uncertainty magnitudes reflecting quantitative prediction errors. Significance: The proposed approach provides a sampling-free and relatively accurate approximation to the multi-pass MC-based uncertainty estimation in the histo-image-based DL PET reconstruction framework. Per-prediction uncertainty quantification enables direct assessment of AI confidence and potentially supports more reliable and informed decision-making.

papers.title: Neural network-based finite-sample transmission coefficient estimation and uncertainty quantification in satellite-to-ground CV-QKD
papers.abstract: Abstract Satellite-to-ground continuous variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) is constrained by rapidly varying free-space channels and short transmission windows, which limit the amount of data available for parameter estimation within each channel interval. Under finite-sample conditions, parameter point estimates are subject to statistical uncertainty and may even yield an overly favorable description of the true channel state, while errors in the estimated transmission coefficient directly affect the covariance matrix used in the security analysis. In this work, we investigate the finite-sample effects of transmission coefficient estimation in dynamic free-space CV-QKD. A neural network is introduced to estimate the transmission coefficient, and the Delta method is used to quantify the uncertainty in its predictions. The proposed method is compared with the standard maximum likelihood estimation method. Confidence intervals for the transmission coefficient are constructed for different sample sizes, and the effects of the statistical uncertainties on the secret key rate are analysed. Under the considered Gaussian-channel simulation conditions, the neural network can provide a more favorable nominal lower bound on the transmission coefficient than MLE in certain sample-limited regimes, leading to a higher parameter-estimation-limited key-rate metric. This work establishes a statistical framework that connects neural network-based transmission coefficient estimation and predictive uncertainty quantification with covariance matrix construction and secret key rate analysis. It provides a basis for machine learning-assisted parameter estimation in free-space CV-QKD systems operating with finite samples.

However, the relationship between dynamics and control has been severed. This work considers the shortcomings of a simplified model of wire rope and studies the dynamic characteristics of an active heave compensation (AHC) system based on flexible wire rope, as well as the control characteristics of an AHC system based on a marine winch. As a result, an AHC method with model predictive control (MPC) based on dynamic simulation results is proposed, which eliminates the sudden displacement of underwater equipment at the start-up moment of the dynamic, reducing the maximum heave displacement from −0.75 to −0.03 m, while the experiments also prove that the AHC system has the ability to reduce maximum heave displacement from 0.95 to 0.025 m. papers.title: Heading-Sensorless Autonomous Vehicles: Luenberger-Based Linear MPC for Tracking and Safe Obstacle Avoidance
papers.abstract: Following a trajectory and avoiding obstacles are two closely linked control tasks for an autonomous vehicle. Classical reactive controllers are tuned for one operating range, do not look ahead and have no built-in way to keep a minimum distance from an obstacle. This paper presents a Linear Time-Invariant Model Predictive Control (LTI-MPC) scheme combined with a Luenberger observer for the kinematic bicycle model. The model is linearised once around (0,0,0,vnom) and written in deviation coordinates so that the drift term of the predictor is exact. The observer, tuned with the discrete-time algebraic Riccati equation, rebuilds the heading from the noisy DGPS-RTK position and odometry speed, so no heading sensor is needed. Static obstacles are handled by a local re-planner with a designed clearance, and a closed-form rule links its blending length to the maximum reference heading. Tested in a closed loop with observer and measurement noise on five scenarios, the LTI-MPC reaches a tracking RMSE of 0.018 m at 4 m/s on a sinusoidal path; achieves, in simulation, a clearance of 0.98–0.99 m from the obstacle (the reference is designed for 1.0 m, the requirement is 0.5 m); and is the only controller among PID-type, Stanley and MPC whose accuracy degrades smoothly from 2 to 8 m/s with a single tuning. The observer converges within 1∘ in 0.24 s. A sweep of constant-radius turns shows that the linearisation stays accurate at up to 30∘ of heading change.

papers.title: Numerical and supervised neural-network analysis of magnetoconvective williamson blood-based Fe₃O₄–Cu hybrid ferrofluid over a moving flat plate
papers.abstract: This study examines the momentum and thermal behavior of a blood-based Williamson hybrid ferrofluid containing magnetite and copper nanoparticles flowing over a moving flat plate in the presence of a transverse magnetic field and viscous dissipation. A steady two-dimensional laminar boundary-layer formulation is considered, together with effective hybrid-fluid properties. The transformed equations are investigated numerically, and a supervised artificial neural network is evaluated as a data-driven surrogate for reference numerical profiles. Unlike a physics-informed neural network, the documented neural loss does not impose differential-equation residuals and boundary conditions. The reported numerical profiles show that increasing the wall-to-free-stream velocity ratio and magnetic parameter increases the plotted velocity, whereas increasing the Williamson parameter decreases it for the chosen cases; temperature increases with the Williamson and Eckert parameters and decreases with the magnetic parameter. The originally reported profile comparisons yield small pointwise differences (typically near 10⁻⁶ in the displayed tables), although these errors are measured against the numerical training reference and are not independent physics validation. The analysis identifies the potential of data-driven prediction for parametric flow studies, while highlighting the need for a consistency-checked non-similar formulation, independent benchmarking, and physically constrained training before PINN performance can be claimed.

papers.title: Stable training and confidence‑calibrated generation of urinary stone CT images via physics‑constrained GANs under small‑sample conditions
papers.abstract: Abstract In recent years, artificial intelligence has become integral to modern medicine. Deep learning algorithms are widely used to assist clinical diagnosis, and medical image synthesis has become increasingly mature. However, in small-sample scenarios, synthetic images often overlook infrequent but clinically valuable lesion features. To address the challenges of training instability, insufficient authenticity, and limited clinical usability, we propose a two-stage framework based on Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). In the first stage, we establish a stable training and physical prior constraint framework for small-sample CT images. Specifically, we incorporate an established asymmetric normalization strategy into the WGAN-GP framework to balance generator convergence and the discriminator's Lipschitz constraint, and we embed a physical noise simulation layer at the discriminator's front end, combined with partial volume effect gradient regularization, to enhance the realism of synthesized images. In the second stage, we employ MC Dropout and deep ensemble methods to quantify uncertainty, generating uncertainty heatmaps and physically consistent confidence maps based on the Poisson-Gaussian noise model. This assists physicians in locating abnormal areas and reducing misdiagnosis risks. Through joint optimization of the generation framework, uncertainty quantification, and confidence image output, the proposed framework effectively resolves issues of mode collapse, low confidence, and poor clinical usability under small-sample conditions. The proposed framework achieves a competitive FID of 128.0, an Expected Calibration Error (ECE) of 0.072, and a high-risk recall rate of 88% for stone boundary regions, demonstrating its potential for clinically reliable synthetic CT generation.

papers.title: Mechanical and Fatigue Properties of a Laser Powder Bed Fusion Ti6Al4V Alloy: A Review
papers.abstract: Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) enables the manufacturing of complex Ti6Al4V components, but the resulting mechanical and fatigue responses are condition-dependent. This critical narrative review examines how alloy grade and interstitial chemistry, powder history, processing, microstructure, residual stress, defect population, surface condition and post-processing affect quasi-static behaviour and low-, high- and very-high-cycle fatigue behaviour. Reported properties are compared with the associated material and test data, including surface condition, build orientation, stress ratio, loading mode, stress definition and run-out criterion. The review distinguishes finite-life fatigue strength from a demonstrated fatigue limit and separates stress-life data from strain-life and crack-growth parameters. The resulting condition-specific synthesis is intended to support engineering comparison and numerical modelling without treating LPBF Ti6Al4V as a single universal material dataset.

papers.abstract: Background: Active learning strategies may improve student engagement and academic performance in medical education. This study compared the effectiveness of multiple-choice question (MCQ)-based small-group teaching with conventional tutorials in undergraduate pathology.Methods: A quasi-experimental crossover study was conducted among 50 second-professional MBBS students at Venkateshwara Institute of Medical Sciences, Uttar Pradesh, during November–December 2024. Students participated in both teaching methods across two pathology topics. Academic performance was assessed through normalized viva-voce scores. Student and faculty perceptions were evaluated using structured Likert-scale questionnaires.Results: Mean viva-voce scores were significantly higher following MCQ-based teaching than conventional tutorials (67.5% versus 53.3%; mean difference 14.2 percentage points; 95% CI 6.4–21.9; p<0.001). Improved performance was observed in 62.0% of students. MCQ-based teaching received significantly more favourable student ratings for clinical reasoning (58.0% versus 40.0%; adjusted p=0.019) and examination preparedness (72.0% versus 58.0%; adjusted p=0.049). Faculty feedback showed no statistically significant differences.Conclusion: MCQ-based small-group teaching was associated with improved viva-voce performance and favourable perceptions of clinical reasoning and examination preparedness, supporting its use as a supplementary pathology teaching strategy.

papers.title: THE PANCHADI LEARNING STEPS IN THE MODERN TEACHING CLASSROOM: A REVIEW OF NCF-SE 2023, TRADITIONAL INDIAN PEDAGOGY AND CONTEMPORARY EVIDENCE
papers.abstract: Modern classrooms are increasingly expected to move beyond traditional lecture-centred approaches towards more learner-centred and outcome-based forms of teaching, as highlighted in India’s National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 and the National Curriculum Framework for School Education (NCF-SE) 2023. In this changing educational landscape, traditional Indian pedagogical practices offer valuable insights into structured and sequential learning, although their potential application in contemporary instructional design has received relatively limited attention. Against this background, the present study examines the Panchadi learning steps, the five-step learning process recommended in the National Curriculum Framework (NCF-FS 2022, integrated within NCF-SE 2023) as a way for teachers to plan the sequence of classroom activities, and explores its conceptual foundations and its relevance to contemporary educational research. The study adopts a narrative review approach, drawing upon NCF policy documents, classical Indian pedagogical texts, foundational theories of learning, and major meta-analyses and research syntheses related to instructional effectiveness. Relevant literature was identified and examined on the basis of its conceptual contribution and methodological significance, followed by thematic organisation and analysis. Although the review does not adopt a PRISMA-based systematic review methodology, selected reporting principles from PRISMA 2020 were considered to improve transparency in the review process. The Panchadi framework, as set out in the NCF, consists of five interconnected steps: Aditi (introduction and connection with prior knowledge), Bodha (conceptual understanding), Abhyāsa (practice), Prayoga (application), and Prasāra (expansion through sharing and communicating learning). The review suggests that these steps share meaningful conceptual connections with several established evidence-based instructional practices, particularly active learning (Freeman et al., 2014; Hake, 1998), retrieval practice (Roediger & Karpicke, 2006), learning by explaining and teaching others (Fiorella & Mayer, 2013), formative assessment and feedback (Black & Wiliam, 1998; Hattie & Timperley, 2007), as well as the 5E and Herbartian instructional models and the classical Indian sequence of śravaṇa, manana and nididhyāsana. Overall, the Panchadi sequence emerges as a culturally rooted and theoretically coherent pedagogical framework with potential applications in contemporary classrooms, including blended and technology-supported learning environments. Nevertheless, the NCF describes Panchadi within its Foundational Stage framework and as a non-binding recommendation, and its actual contribution to teaching and learning outcomes, including at later school stages, needs to be established through further empirical investigation, particularly controlled classroom studies examining its influence on students’ academic achievement, learning engagement, and long-term knowledge retention.

papers.title: Using personas as a tool to explore motivations to join a professional instructor network and the probability of sustained change
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Mentoring is crucial to faculty development; however, not all instructors have access to supportive structures. The Promoting Active Learning and Mentoring (PALM) network facilitated one-on-one faculty mentoring within a structured learning community to encourage active learning. Prior work ( n = 7, only Fellows) created three personas that characterized the range of different Fellows and their motivations for joining the PALM network. Following recruitment from the entire PALM network ( n = 120), both Fellows and Mentors were interviewed ( n = 38) about their interest in joining PALM and their experience in this professional development network. After coding each transcript, we identified three personas: Neil the Novice (limited active learning exposure, lacks role models), Bryn the Budding Expert (experienced implementing active learning, seeking more nuanced approaches, and networking), and Elena the Expert (experienced implementing active learning, integrated into networks, and wants to mentor). Interestingly, features of the previously identified persona, Issa the Isolated (a sense of isolation and a need for external support and validation), were observed in conjunction with two of the three personas—Neil the Novice and Bryn the Budding Expert—but did not form a separate persona. Some individuals reported progression to new personas as a result of participating in PALM. Our findings highlight the importance of supportive networks in helping faculty become more confident instructors. This qualitative analysis of persona development can be used to inform mentoring and other professional development initiatives.

papers.title: Calibrated Uncertainty Quantification for Sectoral Exergy Analysis of Transport Using Probabilistic Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Sectoral exergy studies of transport usually end with a single projected path and no stated uncertainty. In the current study, we develop a calibrated framework to address this and apply it to the Nigerian transport sector. First, we show that exergy-based indicators reduce to one parameter, the subsector exergy efficiency, so that they agree by construction. Next, we forecast fuel demand with an equal weight combination of a Gaussian process trend model and a drift model. Rolling origin backtests show that drift remains the best point forecaster, while the combination gives the best interval score. One scale factor calibrates the 90% intervals to 90.3% coverage, 88.3% on held-out origins, with no widening needed at long horizons. Independent national statistics for 2020 to 2023, never used in fitting, fall inside the 90% intervals in all four years. After updating with these data, Monte Carlo propagation gives 81 Mt of CO2 in 2040 (90% interval 34 to 123 Mt) and an improvement potential of 695 PJ (294 to 1028 PJ). This potential is a thermodynamic upper bound, not an achievable saving. Demand drives almost all CO2 uncertainty. Correlated demand, interactions and changing efficiencies alter them only modestly.

papers.title: Undergraduate nursing students’ perspectives on cooperative learning in the Chinese cultural context: a qualitative descriptive study
papers.abstract: Cooperative learning (CL) is increasingly used in nursing education to promote active learning, communication, and teamwork. Students’ understandings of CL and their related participation behaviors may be shaped by their previous educational experiences and cultural context. This study explored Chinese undergraduate nursing students’ understandings of CL and the behaviors arising from these understandings. A qualitative descriptive study was conducted. Semi-structured interviews were conducted to collect the data. Data collection and analysis were conducted concurrently. Interviews were audio recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using inductive reflexive thematic analysis. The Consolidated criteria for reporting qualitative research (COREQ) checklist was used in this study. Sixteen third-year undergraduate nursing students participated in interviews between March 2024 and April 2024. Three themes and seven subthemes were generated. The first theme, Beneficial but demanding: dual appraisal of CL , reflected students’ recognition of benefits beyond individual learning alongside the complexity of cooperation. The second theme, Actively constructing a workable order , described how students actively participated in CL. The third theme, Simplifying cooperation to avoid extra burdens , showed how students divided collective work and limited in-depth interaction. Chinese undergraduate nursing students’ understandings of CL influenced how they participated and organized cooperation. Nursing educators should consider the influence of students’ previous educational experiences, emphasize the value of CL for developing communication, critical thinking, and teamwork, and strengthen support for individual accountability and group processing. Online collaborative tools may help identify unequal participation and ineffective group processing. Further research should examine these findings in different nursing schools and evaluate educational interventions designed to improve students’ cooperative behaviors. Not applicable.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Photocatalysis: A Systematic Review of Materials Design, Performance Prediction, and Reactor Optimization with Emphasis on Plasmonic Systems
papers.abstract: Plasmonic photocatalysis offers promising alternatives for solar energy conversion, hydrogen production, CO2 reduction, and pollutant degradation. However, its performance depends on multiple variables related to composition, structure, optical and electronic properties, charge transfer, operating conditions, and reactor configuration. This systematic review analyzes the application of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning in photocatalysis, with an emphasis on plasmonic materials, during the period 2020–2026. Using a PRISMA-based methodology, supplemented by bibliometric and technical–comparative analyses, we examined material design and selection, the prediction of photocatalytic performance, reactor optimization, and the construction of datasets. The results show that AI models enable the exploration of compositional and synthetic spaces, the prediction of optical and electronic properties, the optimization of heterojunctions and core–shell structures, and the estimation of H2 production, CO2 conversion, and pollutant degradation, in addition to reducing the computational cost of simulations through surrogate models. Integration with DFT calculations, CFD simulations, active learning, and inverse design expands its application to interconnected predictive and experimental systems. However, limitations persist regarding small and heterogeneous datasets, insufficient external validation, interpretability, and low transferability. Advances in the field will require standardized and traceable data, physically meaningful descriptors, and models that bridge the material, reaction, and reactor scales.

papers.title: Discrete Model-Based Diffusion for Combinatorial Optimization in Multi-Robot Task Allocation
papers.abstract: Decision making in multi-agent and multi-robot systems often involves discrete decision variables, leading to NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems that must be solved within seconds for near real-time implementation. Denoising diffusion has emerged as a powerful tool for such problems, but existing approaches face a trade-off: Model-Based Diffusion (MBD) incorporates diffusion in sampling-based optimization (SBO) without training but only over continuous spaces, while existing diffusion-based combinatorial solvers operate over discrete spaces but require offline training. To this end, we propose Discrete Model-Based Diffusion (Discrete MBD), a training-free SBO method that directly optimizes discrete variables by approximating categorical reverse transition distributions through Monte Carlo sampling. We establish a finite-step lower bound on the probability of finding a global minimizer and show that this bound converges to one as the number of denoising steps increases. Extensive experiments on generic integer programs and heterogeneous multi-robot coalition formation and scheduling demonstrate that Discrete MBD outperforms SBO baselines in nearly all settings while achieving solution quality competitive with that of mixed-integer programming and reinforcement learning methods at a fraction of their computational cost.
