papers.title: Reconstructing Boundary Layer Wind Profiles with Machine Learning: A Comparative Study on IGRA Radiosonde Data
papers.abstract: Wind profiles in the atmospheric boundary layer (ABL) drive short-range forecasting and wind-energy siting, yet sparse radiosonde coverage forces practitioners to interpolate them from a handful of physical predictors. We benchmark modern tabular learners against analytical parameterizations on 158,097 IGRA soundings. CatBoost, TabM, and FT-Transformer reduce RMSE to 1.3-1.6 m/s, against approximately 3 m/s for power-law and Monin-Obukhov fits; once the predictor set is fixed the three architectures differ by less than 0.05 m/s, so accuracy is driven by predictors rather than architecture. A cohort analysis of within-bin profile dispersion places an empirical floor of approximately 1.77 m/s on any point-wise predictor that uses standard radiosonde features, consistent with prior eddy-viscosity inversions. A one-dimensional Fourier Neural Operator applied as a post-hoc corrector to frozen tabular predictions reduces near-surface RMSE on U.S. stations from 1.5 to 1.2 m/s, while leaving upper-layer error unchanged. Further gains should come from new predictors rather than larger models.

papers.title: ProTEUS: A mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution
papers.abstract: Protein engineering requires navigating rugged fitness landscapes, where small sequence changes can produce large functional differences, but experimental screening can only sample a small fraction of sequence space. Thus, a central challenge is to efficiently traverse the large combinatorial space of mutations in silico. We introduce ProTEUS, a mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution. Pretrained on deep mutational scanning assays, ProTEUS learns a joint representation of sequence, evolutionary, and structural information using MutationFormer, a mutation-biased attention architecture. Variants are represented as states in this joint latent space, and mutations define actions whose functional consequences are predicted. To support exploration of many mutants, we developed a fast, physics-constrained all-atom predictor that utilizes explicit geometric constraint enforcement to achieve >10 fold increase in speed than AlphaFold3 with guaranteed physical validity. Lastly, ProTEUS refines its prediction and understanding of protein activity through closed loop experimental feedback to guide evolution toward a desired phenotype. ProTEUS surpasses established models in both zero-shot and supervised fine-tuning mutation prediction tasks. We experimentally demonstrate its utility in two closed-loop multi-objective engineering campaigns on aldehyde dehydrogenase and levansucrase, yielding variants with >10 fold higher activity than wild type. ProTEUS provides a world-model framework that connects virtual evaluation of mutational outcomes with experimental learning for efficient protein evolution.

papers.title: VC-Dimension and Generalization in Geometric Machine Learning with Applications to Active Learning
papers.abstract: We compute the VC-dimension of metric ball classifiers in the model spaces of Riemannian geometry (Euclidean, spherical, hyperbolic) and present upper and lower bounds on the VC-dimension of metric balls in several other situations, including general normed vector spaces (potentially infinite VC-dimension), vector spaces with $\ell^p$-norms (VC-dimension grows at least linearly in the dimension, faster than Euclidean for $p=1$), flat tori, and general Riemannian manifolds (arbitrarily large VC-dimension after a conformal change). In several situations where the VC-dimension is large or even infinite, we prove generalization bounds under additional assumptions on the data distribution using covering arguments. Both in the VC-dimension and covering setting, we consider data on low-dimensional subsets of high-dimensional Euclidean spaces. As an application, we consider coverage-based algorithms in active learning.

papers.title: Multicomponent Isotope Engineering of Phonon Polaritons in Hexagonal Boron Nitride
papers.abstract: Isotopic enrichment provides a non-invasive means of tuning the vibrational and optical properties of van der Waals crystals (vdW) without altering their lattice structure. We investigate two doubly enriched hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) compositions, h10B15N and h11B15N, to determine how isotope substitution on both sublattices modifies mid-infrared hyperbolic phonon polaritons (HPhPs). Polarization-resolved room temperature and cryogenic far-field reflectance measurements reveal optical-phonon blue shifts of approximately 35 cm-1 in h10B15N relative h11B15N, translating both Reststrahlen bands (RBs) and their polariton dispersions. For the upper RB, the combined accessible range expands from 1360-1614 cm-1 in natural hBN to 1356-1640 cm-1 across the B- enriched 14N crystals and 1339-1640 cm-1 when the 15N enriched crystals are included. Near-field imaging confirms deeply sub-diffractional propagation and shows that both crystals exhibit lower polariton damping and longer lifetimes than natural hBN, with performance comparable to monoisotopically enriched crystals. Further, we compare the conventional reduced-mass description with a phenomenological two-component inverse-mass model that captures the isotope dependence of the phonon frequencies and LO-TO coupling while resolving the contributions of the individual sublattices. These results establish multicomponent isotope engineering as a materials design strategy for positioning the HPhPs spectral range while preserving low-loss propagation in polar vdW crystals.

papers.title: Time Series Change Point Detection with Gaussian Processes
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel general Gaussian process framework for change point detection in time series. A change is defined as an alteration of the hyperparameters of the Gaussian process prior. We formulate the problem in the context of statistical hypothesis testing and demonstrate its performance over both offline and online multiple change points detection. The approach provides theoretical guaranties of its performance. An important advantage of the developed framework is that it does not need a detailed specification of the time series function before and after a change. The hyperparameter values are learned from the data. Comprehensive evaluation of the proposed framework is provided both on synthetic and real data and its efficiency is demonstrated.

papers.title: MediPFN: Amortized In-Context Nuisance Learning and Inference for Causal Mediation Analysis
papers.abstract: Causal mediation analysis decomposes a treatment effect into indirect pathways through mediators and direct pathways through other processes. Tabular foundation models perform classification and regression through in-context learning, providing estimates of conditional means and propensity scores used in causal mediation analysis. Constructing confidence intervals from these estimates requires accounting for uncertainty introduced by fitting and combining several nuisance functions. We introduce MediPFN, an amortized inference framework that adapts a pretrained tabular foundation model to nuisance prediction and combines its predictions through a cross-fitted influence-function estimator. A separate head learns quantiles of the estimator's standardized error from simulated tables with known indirect effects. Supervised fine-tuning, symmetrization, and independent calibration then produce a confidence interval. We establish coverage bounds for the resulting intervals under standard assumptions. Across experiments, MediPFN attains coverage closer to the nominal level than several comparators. It also reduces the computational cost of uncertainty quantification, running 59.1 times faster than bootstrap in matched comparisons.

papers.title: Prediction Inference for Hybrid Models on Realized Volatility Forecasting
papers.abstract: GARCH-LSTM hybrid models have become increasingly popular in the volatility forecasting literature. To date, these models have almost exclusively focused on point estimation and accuracy measures such as RMSE and MAPE, while failing to assess the uncertainty of these point estimates. We approach this gap in two ways. First, we extend the existing GARCH-LSTM model by modeling the conditional mean with an ARMA structure. Second, we develop a forward bootstrap algorithm to build multi-step-ahead prediction intervals for future realized volatility. In order to address the notorious undercoverage of prediction intervals, we implement two solutions. One draws bootstrap innovations from the empirical residual distribution to mimic the fat-tail property of financial series. The other utilizes principles from conformal prediction to systematically extend the prediction interval length. We evaluate the methods in simulations with heavy-tailed and time-varying GARCH processes and in rolling-window forecasts of four U.S. stock indices from 2020 to 2025. The ARMA-based hybrid gives the lowest point-forecast errors in most settings, and combining both remedies with the mean-based hybrid yields intervals closest to the nominal level among competing methods.

papers.title: Ground Reaction Force-Aware Model Predictive Control for Underactuated Upright Physical Assistance
papers.abstract: Many rehabilitation robots execute prescribed motions using reactive tracking controllers that do not explicitly incorporate the user's instantaneous human-ground interaction. This paper presents Ground Reaction Force-Aware Model Predictive Control (GRF-MPC), a framework for upright physical assistance. By integrating live GRF and center of pressure (CoP) measurements directly into a human centroidal dynamics model, GRF-MPC formulates a real-time quadratic program (QP) that optimizes assistive forces and moments over a receding horizon. We deployed GRF-MPC on the Robotic Upright Stand Trainer (RobUST) in an underactuated 4-cable configuration and evaluated it against a fully actuated 8-cable Cartesian impedance baseline in nearly 300 trials across six healthy participants. Across tasks spanning impulsive perturbations, lunge trajectories, and voluntary limits of stability, GRF-MPC reduced peak planar center-of-mass (CoM) error by 19.6% during perturbations, lowered trajectory tracking error by 24.1%, required 28.7% less net mechanical work, and permitted a 45.9% greater normalized voluntary excursion area. The underlying QP solves in under 1 ms, comfortably enabling 100 Hz replanning and demonstrating that incorporating live human-ground interaction into predictive control yields stronger, more transparent physical assistance with half the actuators.

papers.title: Audited Gradients, Anchored Policies: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning for Efficient Flow Control
papers.abstract: Feedback controllers for flows are expensive to design, since each candidate must be evaluated with a high-fidelity solver. Differentiable surrogates reduce that cost, but they also introduce a failure mode that prediction error cannot detect. Policy optimization uses the derivative of the objective with respect to the action, which we call the action gradient and which can be computed either through the surrogate or through the high-fidelity solver. Optimization through the surrogate uses only its action gradient, and a surrogate can follow the flow trajectory closely while misestimating this derivative. The surrogate action gradient is compared against a central finite-difference estimate from the high-fidelity solver on held-out states, under acceptance criteria fixed before the comparison, and we call that comparison an audit. A low-dimensional feedback law is then fitted to the surrogate action gradient when the surrogate passes the audit, and to the solver estimate when it does not. This law initializes a neural policy, and a quadratic penalty holds the policy near it during optimization. The proposed approach is validated on four test cases. The resulting controllers outperform or match a model-free baseline, while using 3 to 156 times fewer high-fidelity solver interactions across the four test cases. One surrogate predicts the objective at correlation 0.9996 but its action gradient at only 0.459, so prediction accuracy does not identify a usable surrogate. Another surrogate, whose action gradient agrees with the solver estimate at correlation 0.996, makes the objective 0.52% worse when the policy is optimized through it without the anchor penalty, so an accurate gradient alone does not provide a working controller. Finally, a surrogate that passes the audit at one fixed action fails it around the actions the deployed controller applies, so a pass is local.

papers.title: Building World Models from Intrinsic Motivation
papers.abstract: In the absence of extrinsic rewards or task supervision, human behavior is guided by intrinsic motivation---neural signals that drive curiosity, creativity, play, and other essential facets of intelligence. Intrinsic motivation plays an important developmental role in building robust world models that enable generalization and adaptation. Yet existing studies leave open how a broad range of intrinsic motivations interacts with world-model representation learning to support downstream control. This limits our understanding of which intrinsically collected experiences build reusable models. To address these gaps, we integrate 24 intrinsic objectives, including established methods and explicit variants spanning curiosity, entropy, and competency, into a common model-based reinforcement learning framework. We evaluate the world models they build through zero-shot, few-shot, and multi-task control in locomotion, manipulation, and open-ended gaming environments, using three representation-learning strategies: observation reconstruction, latent prediction, and redundancy reduction. Curiosity-driven exploration with observation reconstruction yields the strongest aggregate family profile, although the best individual pairing depends on the experiment. In compositional vision-based tasks, intrinsic motivation derived from both episodic and lifelong novelty---providing a complementary memory to the world model's generic recurrent state---achieves the best zero-shot transfer and few-shot adaptation. These findings motivate designing intrinsic motivation and representation learning jointly. Our results demonstrate world models as a powerful tool for measuring the quality of intrinsically motivated experience, and positions intrinsic motivation as a key ingredient for building world models autonomously.

papers.title: Predictive Modelling of Ultimate Tensile Strength in Similar and Dissimilar AA2050-AA7475 Friction Stir Welds Using Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Abstract Aerospace-grade heat-treatable aluminium alloys are often joined using solid-state welding processes such as friction stir welding (FSW). However, limited research has examined dissimilar AA2050-AA7475 joints. In this study, various machine learning (ML) models are developed to predict the ultimate tensile strength (UTS) of similar (AA2050–AA2050, AA7475–AA7475) and dissimilar (AA2050–AA7475) FSW joints. A dataset of 108 experimental trials was generated using six process parameters: tilt angle, shoulder diameter, rotational speed, pin diameter, tool offset, and traverse speed. Five ML models, such as Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Support Vector Regressor (SVR), Random Forest Regression (RFR), XGBoost, and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), were evaluated using pooled out-of-fold cross-validation. XGBoost achieved the highest prediction accuracy (R² = 0.761), while GPR (R² = 0.718) was selected for its ability to model continuous variations and estimate prediction uncertainty. Joint type was the most influential factor affecting UTS. Optimal performance was observed with a tool offset of 0.5–0.75 mm, rotational speed of 700–900 rpm for dissimilar joints, and traverse speed of 180–220 mm/min for similar joints. GPR validation showed a MAPE of 2.1%, with all predictions within ±5% of experimental values, confirming its reliability.

papers.title: A novel zero-shot bearing fault diagnosis method based on physics-informed digital twin model and domain-alignment strategy
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper proposes a novel zero-shot bearing fault diagnosis method that tackles the critical challenge of data scarcity, a long-standing bottleneck in fault diagnosis, particularly for industrial applications.By integrating a physics-informed digital twin (PIDT) model with a domain-alignment strategy (DAS), the proposed method generates high-fidelity virtual vibration signals that comply with the inherent physical dynamics of bearing systems, and effectively aligns the noisy real-world signals with the virtual signals. The PIDT model fuses a 4-DOF bearing dynamic model with a neural network, incorporating two complementary loss functions: a physical residual loss, which enforces consistency with the governing physical equations, and a frequency prior loss that guarantees spectral fidelity. The DAS bridges the domain discrepancy between noise-free virtual data and real-world measured signals by aligning the real-world signals with the virtual domain. This integrated framework thereby enables reliable fault classification even without labeled fault data during model training. Experimental results validate the method's robustness and generalizability, achieving average zero-shot diagnostic accuracies of 95.53±1.46% on a self-built test rig and 95.15±1.89% on the CWRU dataset, respectively, significantly outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods in both accuracy and stability across various operational conditions. Furthermore, ablation studies rigorously validate the critical contributions of both the PIDT's loss components and the DAS in to the zero-shot performance. The proposed method provides an effective solution to the data scarcity dilemma in bearing fault diagnosis and offers significant potential for real-world industrial applications.

papers.title: Discrete‐Time Caputo Fractional‐Order Terminal Sliding Mode Control for Uncertain MIMO Systems Using Multi‐Agent Reinforcement Learning With Disturbance Compensation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper proposes a novel data‐driven discrete‐time control framework for uncertain nonlinear MIMO systems by integrating discrete‐time Caputo fractional‐order terminal sliding mode control, multi‐agent reinforcement learning and reinforcement learning‐based disturbance compensation. Unlike existing discrete‐time fractional‐order sliding mode controllers that rely on accurate system models and fixed controller parameters, the proposed framework simultaneously achieves adaptive controller optimisation and online disturbance compensation using only input‐output measurements, thereby eliminating the dependence on precise mathematical modelling. A discrete‐time Caputo fractional‐order terminal sliding surface is developed to guarantee finite‐time convergence while preserving the memory characteristics of fractional‐order dynamics. To improve robustness against external disturbances and internal uncertainties, a reinforcement learning‐based disturbance observer is designed to estimate and compensate for unknown perturbations in real time. Furthermore, a multi‐agent reinforcement learning strategy is employed to adaptively optimise the controller gains without manual parameter tuning, resulting in enhanced tracking performance under varying operating conditions. The closed‐loop stability of the proposed controller is rigorously established using Lyapunov theory for discrete‐time fractional‐order systems. Comparative simulation studies conducted on a benchmark nonlinear MIMO system demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves a 14.54% reduction in the integral of absolute error (IAE) under the model uncertainty‐only scenario compared with the conventional fractional‐order sliding mode controller. Furthermore, additional simulation results under combined model uncertainties and external disturbances confirm the superior robustness, adaptive capability and tracking accuracy of the proposed framework.

papers.title: Adaptive stability boundary-based model predictive control for vehicle lateral stability under low-adhesion conditions
papers.abstract: To address the nonlinear instability of vehicles under extreme operating conditions such as high speed, low road adhesion, and large steering angles, this paper establishes a lateral–yaw dynamics model considering tire nonlinear characteristics. The effects of longitudinal vehicle speed, front-wheel steering angle, and road adhesion coefficient on vehicle chaotic bifurcation behavior and phase-plane stability boundaries are analyzed. Based on a phase-plane point-set identification method, an adaptive stability region varying with operating conditions is constructed and transformed into a state constraint for model predictive control. Accordingly, a boundary-constrained model predictive control method incorporating nonlinear stability boundaries, referred to as BMPC, is proposed. In addition, the local stability of the system near equilibrium points is analyzed using the Lyapunov method. Co-simulation and hardware-in-the-loop test results demonstrate that the proposed BMPC method can effectively prevent the vehicle states from entering unstable regions. Under complex road conditions and extreme handling scenarios, the method achieves improved path-tracking accuracy, lateral stability, and robustness. The results provide theoretical support and engineering guidance for stability control of intelligent vehicles under complex driving conditions.

papers.title: Anisotropic performance of FDM-printed ABS/MWCNT nanocomposites: Investigating the influence of production direction on mechanical properties and electrical conductivity
papers.abstract: With the development of additive manufacturing technologies, lattice structures capable of simultaneously providing lightweight characteristics, high specific strength, and functional properties have gained increasing importance in engineering applications. In particular, the use of electrically conductive composite filaments offers new opportunities in areas such as health monitoring, piezoresistive sensing, and smart engineering systems. In such applications, structures are required to possess not only adequate electrical performance but also reliable mechanical strength. However, the anisotropic behavior resulting from the layered structure of parts produced by the Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) process causes both mechanical and electrical properties to vary depending on the build orientation. In this study, the mechanical and electrical performances of TPMS (Triply Periodic Minimal Surface)-based Gyroid, Diamond, and Schwarz lattice structures fabricated by the FDM process using ABS matrix filaments reinforced with MWCNTs (Multi-Walled Carbon Nanotubes) were investigated. Compression tests, surface hardness measurements, and electrical resistance measurements were conducted on specimens manufactured in different build orientations (XY and Z). The analysis and characterization results demonstrated that TPMS topology, MWCNT content, and build orientation have significant effects on the performance of the structures. The highest electrical conductivity value, 0.0257 S/m, was obtained for the Gyroid specimens containing 1% MWCNT and manufactured in the Z orientation. As the MWCNT content increased to 3% and 5%, a significant decrease in conductivity values was observed, which was associated with nanotube agglomeration and the disruption of conductive network continuity at higher filler contents. Furthermore, it was determined that build orientation induced considerable anisotropy in electrical behavior, resulting in conductivity differences approaching two hundredfold between the Z and XY orientations in some specimens. When the mechanical and electrical results were evaluated together, the Gyroid geometry exhibited a more balanced and stable performance, and it was revealed that TPMS topology and build orientation are critical parameters in the design of multifunctional composite structures.

papers.title: Synthesis Route‐Controlled Atomic Ordering Optimizes Thermoelectric Transport in Bi 2 SbSe 3
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Thermoelectrics have leveraged band and phonon engineering to optimize performance, typically realized through chemical composition control via one‐pot doping or alloying. However, for compounds with complex atomic sites, the thermodynamic drive of conventional one‐pot synthesis generally favors a thermodynamically preferred atomic occupation, thereby limiting atomic ordering control and obscuring its influence on thermoelectric transport. Herein, we constructed a synthetic pathway for composition‐invariant band and phonon engineering via atomic ordering control in one‐third Sb‐alloyed BiSe (Bi 2 SbSe 3 ), a compound with multiple crystallographically distinct cation sites. Using BiSbSe 3 and Bi powders as precursors, we synthesized more disordered Bi 2 SbSe 3 than the one‐pot synthesized counterpart, achieved by redistributing Sb atoms between the Bi 2 Se 3 quintuple layers and the Bi bilayers in the BiSe structure. Reduced atomic ordering suppresses the higher‐lying conduction band contribution, lowering effective mass and enhancing carrier mobility, while simultaneously triggering lattice structure, slowing phonon velocities, and reducing lattice thermal conductivity. Finally, decreased atomic ordering enhances the ZT value of Bi 2 SbSe 3 by ∼15% to ∼0.61 at 423 K, with an energy conversion efficiency of ∼4.3% under a temperature difference of ∼323 K. These results reveal that synthesis‐controlled atomic ordering is an effective strategy for enhancing thermoelectric performance in structurally complex materials.

papers.title: Robust multivariable control for enhanced microalgae biomass and lipid productivity in continuous photobioreactors (Robust multivariable control in continuous microalgae photobioreactors)
papers.abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Microalgae have high potential as a primary source (lipids and carbohydrates) for sustainable energy production ( e.g. biodiesel, biogas, bioethanol) and high‐value biomass secondary products (feed and nutrient supplements). High production costs are the main barrier to commercializing microalgal‐derived biofuels. Thus, various methods have been proposed to enhance microalgal biomass and lipid content. This paper addresses enhancements in lipid and biomass productivity in microalgal continuous photobioreactors using nonlinear programming optimization and two robust control approaches. RESULTS The favorable selection of the dilution rate and the input nutrient concentration as manipulable variables, along with the design of controllers using robust nonlinear model predictive control and modeling error compensation approaches, leads to reliable and efficient multivariable control approaches aimed at improving biomass and lipid productivities in microalgae photobioreactors simultaneously. Numerical simulations of the proposed control approaches demonstrate good and robust closed‐loop performance under significant model uncertainties and external perturbations. CONCLUSIONS Two robust controllers with simple design and structure are introduced to address underlying uncertainties in the mathematical models of microalgae photobioreactors. The proposed control schemes enable simultaneous manipulation of the dilution rate and substrate input concentration to enhance lipid and biomass productivities. © 2026 The Author(s). papers.title: FROM GENERATIVE AI TO AGENTIC LEARNING SYSTEMS: A HUMANAI COLLABORATION FRAMEWORK FOR THE FUTURE OF DISTANCE HIGHER EDUCATION
papers.abstract: Generative AI entered universities as a tool that students consult on demand. The next generation of systems, AI agents that plan, remember and act over several steps, will take over parts of teaching, and distance education will feel this first. This article asks how responsibility should be divided between people and such agents in distance higher education. Following design science methodology, it combines an integrative review of experimental and survey evidence published in 2019-2026, regulatory documents and enrolment data for Uzbekistan. The evidence points in one direction: the same models raise or lower learning depending on how they are constrained. An AI tutor built around expert-written scaffolding produced learning gains 0.73 to 1.3 standard deviations larger than active learning in class, while unrestricted GPT-4 access raised practice scores by 48% but lowered later exam scores by 17%. Student use of AI is close to universal (92-95% in UK surveys, 60-72% in Uzbek samples), yet only about a third of students report receiving institutional training. In Uzbekistan, correspondence and distance students account for 32% of 1.85 million students, with 36 students per teacher. The proposed framework defines five levels of AI agency, from tool to orchestrating agent, and assigns each distance learning task a maximum level using three criteria: the stakes of the decision, the reversibility of errors and the strength of evidence. Tutoring and formative feedback may reach the tutor agent level under teacher oversight, whereas grading, progression and admission remain human decisions. Recommendations for universities and national AI policy follow.

papers.title: DATA-DRIVEN ADAPTIVE MODEL PREDICTIVE CONTROL FOR CONSTRAINED NON LINEAR SYSTEMS
papers.abstract: Electronic throttle systems (ETS) combine a DC motor, a gearbox, a limp-home return spring, Coulomb friction and airflow torque, and must track the commanded plate angle within a 0–24 V supply. The base paper of this thesis (Youssef, Wafa and Shalaby, 2025) addresses this with an Adaptive Relaxed Sliding Mode Controller (ARSMC) in which a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) actor–critic agent adapts the lumped-uncertainty bound, shrinking the boundary layer that removes chattering. This thesis reproduces the ETS model and the SMC, RSMC and ARSMC controllers of the base paper and extends the work with an offset-free Model Predictive Controller (MPC). The MPC feedbacklinearises the throttle, estimates angle, speed and the lumped disturbance with a third-order extended state observer (ESO), and solves a 40-variable box-constrained quadratic program every 5 ms, so the 0– 24 V limit is enforced inside the optimisation rather than by clipping. All controllers are compared in MATLAB on the same staircase reference (0.4, 0.8 and 1.5 rad), parametric uncertainty and airflow disturbance, in three scenarios: uncertainty inside the design bound, uncertainty 50% above it, and 2 mrad sensor noise. Compared with ARSMC, the proposed MPC reduces the integral absolute error by 39%, 36% and 78%, the integral squared error by 37%, 34% and 73%, and the rise time by 41%, 38% and 78% in the three scenarios, with zero steady-state error and a chatter-free voltage. Its cost is a 4–6 mrad overshoot, which ARSMC avoids. The MPC needs no training and solves its QP in about 0.6 ms.

papers.title: Dynamic Epistemic–Temporal Graph Reasoning With Uncertainty Calibration for Evidence-Consistent Forensic Interrogation Narratives
papers.abstract: Forensic interrogation narratives are dynamic and evolve over time, across claims, events, locations, and evidential sources, so statement-level analysis alone is inadequate to support the reliability assessment of claimed consistency.The proposed dynamic epistemic-temporal graph reasoning framework with uncertainty calibration for evidence-consistent forensic interrogation narratives aims to provide a robust framework for generating forensic interrogation narratives that are evidence-consistent and incorporate uncertainty.It combines ModernBERT for contextual language representation, DeBERTa-v3 as a natural language inference model to model support and contradiction, a Dynamic Epistemic-Temporal Heterogeneous Graph Transformer for multi-hop reasoning, and conformal prediction to provide uncertainty-aware decision support.Interrogation discourse becomes structured representations of claims, entities, events, temporal expressions, locations, and relations of evidence.These elements are embedded in a dynamic heterogeneous graph that represents semantic, temporal, and evidential relationships between elements of the evolving story.The proposed Dynamic Epistemic-Temporal Heterogeneous Graph Transformer aims to detect inconsistencies that might not be captured by single-or two-part analysis, especially when evidence is spread across various claims, events, time references, places, and sources of evidence.Natural language inference facilitates semantic relation assessment, and temporal reasoning deals with event order, duration, overlap, and timeline compatibility.Conformal prediction is used to separate reliable consistency judgments from cases that are more ambiguous and require human review.It goes beyond the classification of deception and provides a framework of dynamic, evidence-based narrative reasoning designed to complement, not supplant, expert forensic judgment.The evaluation emphasizes evidence-consistency classification, semantic, temporal, evidential, and multi-hop reasoning, as well as uncertainty calibration.The future goals of crossdataset generalization and real-world robustness are left for future work.

papers.title: Sustainable fibre-reinforced polymer composites for biomedical applications
papers.abstract: Fibre-reinforced polymers (FRPs) are promising alternatives to metallic and monolithic polymeric implants because their stiffness, strength and degradation can be tailored through fibre type, matrix chemistry, fibre fraction and architecture. This review examines mechanical performance, biocompatibility, and emerging design trends, and grades the evidence for each system from clinical to purely computational. Stiffness matching is the central mechanical rationale: cortical bone (~14 GPa) is ~7.9 times less stiff than Ti-6Al-4V (~110 GPa) but only ~1.3 times less stiff than carbon-fibre-reinforced PEEK (CFR-PEEK, ~18 GPa); a simplified iso-strain estimate gives implant axial load shares of ~89%, ~56% and ~32% for titanium, CFR-PEEK and a glass/sisal/chitosan sandwich (tensile modulus 6.6 GPa), respectively. Clinical evidence for CFR-PEEK in trauma remains of low certainty (nine studies, 431 patients; standardized mean difference in function 0.22, 95% CI −0.03 to 0.47). Architecture and nano-reinforcement can add measurable but system-specific gains: spatial versus planar Bouligand carbon-fibre/hydroxyapatite gave +85.6% compressive and +38.4% flexural strength, whereas 2 wt.% graphene oxide raised the modulus of a polyhydroxyalkanoate film by 36% and 0.5 wt.% cellulose nanofibre raised PLA modulus by 18.4% at a 7.4% strength loss. Natural-fibre bone-plate concepts show in-vitro cell viability up to 96.7% at 72 h and inhibition zones up to 28 mm, but no animal or clinical data, strong moisture sensitivity, and almost no fatigue data in physiological media; in 3D-printed PLA scaffolds, the compressive strength was largely unchanged after 30 days in Hanks' solution, while fatigue resistance decreased significantly. The sterilization effects are material-specific, and most advanced concepts (Bouligand, 4D, machine-learning design) remain laboratory or computational. Three priorities follow from the quantified gaps: fatigue and property retention in physiological media, degradation-matched mechanical and biological safety, and standardized evidence for clinical translation.

papers.title: Application of the Realistic Mathematics Education (RME) Approach to Improve Numeracy Skills
papers.abstract: This study aimed to improve students’ numeracy skills through the implementation of the Realistic Mathematics Education (RME) approach in learning multiplication and division of whole numbers in Grade III at SD 2 Karangbener. The study employed Classroom Action Research conducted in two cycles. Each cycle consisted of two meetings involving planning, action, observation, and reflection stages. The participants were 11 third-grade students. The data included students’ numeracy skills, learning activities, and teacher teaching skills. The results showed that the average numeracy score increased from 37.36 in the initial condition to 73.27 in Cycle I and 80.64 in Cycle II. Classical mastery increased from 9.09% to 54.55% and reached 81.82% in Cycle II. Student learning activity increased from 80% in Cycle I to 92.5% in Cycle II, while teacher teaching skills increased from 75% to 87.5%. The implementation of RME provided contextual learning experiences that helped students connect mathematical concepts with meaningful situations, supporting the development of numeracy skills and active learning in elementary education.

papers.title: EFEKTIVITAS PENGGUNAAN MODEL PEMBELAJARAN STUDENT FASILITATOR AND EXPLAINING DALAM PELAJARAN PPKn PADA SISWA SMA SWASTA MUHAMMADIYAH 11 PADANGSIDIMPUAN TAHUN PELAJARAN 2025-2026
papers.abstract: Civic Education (PPKn) lessons are still often teacher-centered, so student participation tends to be limited. This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of the Student Facilitator and Explaining (SFAE) cooperative learning model compared to conventional learning in improving civic education learning outcomes of students at Muhammadiyah 11 Private High School Padangsidimpuan for the 2025/2026 school year. The research uses a quantitative approach with a comparative experimental method and a posttest-only control group design. The study population included all 42 students in grades 10 and 11, who were then selected as the sample using total sampling. Grade 11, consisting of 20 students, received the SFAE model treatment, while grade 10, consisting of 22 students, received conventional learning. The data was collected through an objective test on Civics learning outcomes and analyzed using an independent sample t-test. The analysis results showed that the average learning outcome of the SFAE group was 80.25, categorized as very good, while the conventional group had an average of 66.59, categorized as sufficient. The t-test resulted in a t-value of 14.767, which is greater than the t-table value of 1.684 at a 0.05 significance level. Thus, the SFAE model proved to be more effective than conventional learning in improving Civics learning outcomes. These findings suggest the use of SFAE as an alternative active learning method that engages students in explaining, discussing, and collaboratively constructing understanding.

papers.title: Strategi pengembangan kompetensi guru pendidikan agama Islam di Sekolah Menengah Pertama
papers.abstract: This study aimed to analyze strategies for developing the competencies of Islamic Religious Education teachers to improve instructional quality at Chandra Buana Junior High School in Bogor. The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach. Data were collected through interviews, observations, and document analysis, with the school principal and Islamic Religious Education teachers serving as the key informants. The findings revealed that teacher competency development was implemented systematically, through structured programs, and on a continuous basis by strengthening four core competencies: pedagogical, personality, professional, and social competencies. Pedagogical competence was developed through annual training and workshops, the preparation of lesson plans and teaching modules, the implementation of active learning models, the improvement of formative and summative assessment practices, and academic supervision. Personality competence was strengthened through regular religious study sessions, the habituation of Islamic values, the development of a religious school culture, and teacher role modelling. Professional competence was enhanced through subject-matter development, training, reflective teaching practices, academic supervision, professional collaboration, and participation in the Subject Teacher Forum (Musyawarah Guru Mata Pelajaran or MGMP). Social competence was developed through interpersonal communication training, workshops, internal professional development forums, communication with parents, and participation in school-based social and religious activities. The study concludes that the integrated development of these four competencies contributes to improving the professionalism of Islamic Religious Education teachers and fostering effective, contextual, and humanistic learning that promotes character development and enhances instructional quality. Abstrak Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis strategi pengembangan kompetensi Guru Pendidikan Agama Islam (PAI) dalam meningkatkan mutu pembelajaran di SMP Chandra Buana Bogor. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan metode deskriptif. Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara, observasi, dan studi dokumentasi dengan kepala sekolah dan Guru PAI sebagai informan utama. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa pengembangan kompetensi Guru PAI dilaksanakan secara sistematis, terprogram, dan berkelanjutan melalui penguatan kompetensi pedagogik, kepribadian, profesional, dan sosial. Kompetensi pedagogik dikembangkan melalui pelatihan dan workshop tahunan, penyusunan perangkat pembelajaran, penerapan model pembelajaran aktif, penguatan asesmen formatif dan sumatif, serta supervisi akademik. Kompetensi kepribadian diperkuat melalui kajian keagamaan, pembiasaan nilai-nilai Islam, budaya religius sekolah, dan keteladanan guru. Kompetensi profesional dikembangkan melalui pendalaman materi, pelatihan, refleksi pembelajaran, supervisi akademik, kolaborasi antar guru, dan kegiatan Musyawarah Guru Mata Pelajaran. Sementara itu, kompetensi sosial dikembangkan melalui pelatihan komunikasi interpersonal, workshop, forum pembinaan internal, komunikasi dengan orang tua, serta keterlibatan dalam kegiatan sosial dan keagamaan sekolah. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa integrasi pengembangan keempat kompetensi tersebut berkontribusi terhadap peningkatan profesionalisme Guru PAI dan terciptanya pembelajaran yang efektif, kontekstual, humanis, serta berorientasi pada pembentukan karakter dan peningkatan mutu pembelajaran.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该文研究伊斯兰宗教教育教师能力发展策略，与FEA代理建模、生物力学或植入物设计完全无关。
llm.why_not_core: This is a qualitative education-management study with no simulation, surrogate modeling, optimization, uncertainty quantification, or biomechanics content whatsoever.

summary_zh.motivation: 探讨如何通过教师能力发展提升伊斯兰宗教教育教学质量。
summary_zh.method: 采用描述性定性方法，通过访谈、观察和文档分析收集数据。
summary_zh.result: 发现学校通过系统化项目持续强化教学、人格、专业与社会四类能力。
summary_zh.validation: 基于单校案例的定性证据，无定量或仿真验证。

summary_en.motivation: The study seeks to understand how Islamic religious education teachers' competencies can be systematically developed to raise instructional quality.
summary_en.method: A descriptive qualitative design was used, drawing on interviews, classroom observations, and document analysis at a single junior high school.
summary_en.result: Competency development was found to be implemented through structured, continuous programs targeting pedagogical, personality, professional, and social competencies.
summary_en.validation: Evidence is limited to qualitative case data from one school, with no quantitative or computational validation.
